title: Members on Kolkata and other cities · AquaTerra
description: AquaTerra members write about Kolkata and other cities: old clock shops, a cab ride across town, the Patna heat and a city seen from a plane.
lede: AquaTerra's members write about the cities they know: a lane between a bookstore and a small church in Kolkata, an afternoon in the Patna heat, and a city seen from the window of a plane. This page is a reading guide to those pieces, and to the drives that take our students out onto the same streets.

sections.heading: the streets people write about
body: The most personal piece here is Letter to My City, which is written as a letter to the city itself. It starts in the old, labyrinth-like streets of Kolkata, somewhere between a forgotten bookstore and a small church, where an old clock shop has been known for generations. The details are small and specific, and that is what makes the city feel real: a lane nobody on a main road would notice, and a shop that has been there for years.

Before you Judge Read This is set on a quiet afternoon during a cab ride across the city. It is about how quickly we rush to judge the people we pass, and what changes when we stop and hear the full story. A Tale of Two Cities starts somewhere else entirely, with a flight announcement as the plane lands in Boston, so it opens with the moment of arriving in a new place.

sections.heading: other cities, other kinds of heat
body: Cup of Tea is set in Patna, where the sun is melting the city down and a man's son takes him to a nearby temple. The son goes off to buy a few sweets. It is a slow, small story about an afternoon, not a travel piece, and it shows how much of a city is in its ordinary errands.

Restock My Fridge opens with a picture of a particular kind of city life: a twenty-step hand care routine, cans of Diet Coke by the case, and a downtown loft in New York or Miami. Read it as a question about which version of a city we are told to want, and whether it is anything like the city people in Kolkata actually live in.

sections.heading: from reading the city to working in it
body: The writing here is about the same city where AquaTerra's drives happen. Book Basket collections have gone to neighbourhoods such as Ballygunge and Lake Town, and to housing complexes across Kolkata. A member who writes about a lane is writing about the kind of place our teams walk into on a drive day.

Our suggestion is simple. Read a piece like Letter to My City, then walk a route you know with fresh eyes. If you want to see more of the city from the inside, join a drive. [How a drive works](/impact/how-a-drive-works) explains what happens on one, from the plan to the write-up that goes on this site.

learnings: A city is easier to understand through its smallest streets than through its landmarks.
Specific details, a clock shop, a temple visit, a plate of sweets, carry more of a place than a list of neighbourhoods.
Pausing before judging a stranger in a crowded city is a habit worth practising, as Before you Judge Read This suggests.
Writing about your own city is a good way to start noticing the things you would otherwise walk past.

faqs.q: Where can I read AquaTerra members writing about Kolkata?
faqs.a: AquaTerra members write about Kolkata and other cities on Groundwork Diaries, the students' writing on this site. Letter to My City is set in Kolkata, and Cup of Tea is set in Patna.

faqs.q: What is Letter to My City about?
faqs.a: Letter to My City is a piece by an AquaTerra member, written as a letter to Kolkata. It opens in the old, winding streets of the city, between a forgotten bookstore and a small church, where a clock shop has been known for generations.

faqs.q: Do AquaTerra members write about cities outside Kolkata?
faqs.a: Yes. Cup of Tea is set in Patna, and A Tale of Two Cities opens on a flight landing in Boston. AquaTerra's drives themselves happen in Kolkata, and the impact library lists the drive series and where they ran.

faqs.q: Where does AquaTerra run its drives in Kolkata?
faqs.a: AquaTerra runs drives across Kolkata, in neighbourhoods such as Ballygunge and Lake Town, at housing complexes, and at places we keep going back to. Each drive series has its own page in the [impact library](/impact) with the places and years it ran.

faqs.q: How can a teenager in Kolkata join AquaTerra?
faqs.a: AquaTerra is a free, student-run registered charitable trust for members aged 14 to 19. You join by signing in with Google and waiting for an approval, then take part in drives across the city. [Join AquaTerra](/join) to start.
